chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Nasr, from Jameel, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the cursing man and the cursing woman, how should they both be dealt with? He (peace be upon him) said: 'The Imam (peace be upon him) would sit with his back towards the Qiblah, so he would place both of them in front of him facing the Qiblah, aligned with him, and he would begin with the man, then the woman, and the woman upon whom stoning is obligated, would be stoned from behind her back, and would not be stoned from her face, because the striking and the stoning do not hit the face; they are struck upon the body, upon all of the parts.'

key_terms.الْمُلَاعَنَةِ: The cursing woman (wife accused by husband)
key_terms.الْمُلَاعِنِ: The cursing man (husband who accuses wife of adultery without witnesses)

ai.seo_question: What is the ritual procedure for the cursing (Khassafayn) procedure in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the procedural mechanics of *Li'an* (cursing), where the Imam presides with his back to the Qibla while the husband and wife face it, ensuring the ritual's solemnity and distinctness from prayer. It further clarifies the physical application of punishment, noting that stoning (*Rajm*) and flogging are directed at the body rather than the face, a nuance significant in Shia fiqh for preserving dignity during corporal punishment.
